div.p: md the head command from initial object is at top of file, so it is equal.
head will always be less than or equal to the file.
the tail operation, this allows a dual operation that has less than relations that cohere with head.
So the tail has a preorder, and the head that remains valid up to an operation leaving with a terminal object.
this means the head and tail operation are preserved. in order to maintain this operation, both head and tail with use the + operation so that the morphism to the boundary position can compose.

These operations are abstract enough toe be like 'head or tail' in functional programming, however, category theory allows you to more naturally define all operations as closed symmetric monoidial category.

p.strong: Capability: Document Explainations at the speed of thought

li.p: use fragments of source files (markdown, code, etc) to be easily added as nodes to a diagram
actualise diagrams in markdowns from within vim... render d2 codeblock and add as an image block

ul.li: a system to define a catalogue of coherent literate objects that can be composed
allow natural writing workflow to map realisation to actualisation

div.p: communication capabilities: describe an action and what it does, this gets map to providing an example, and is documented such that it can be played with
